column1: PART 1: PROBLEM DEFINITION (Challenges Faced by Indian Farmers)

column3: Traditional flood irrigation wastes 30% to 40% of fresh groundwater due to evaporation and uncontrolled field flooding because farmers lack visual root-zone moisture data and crop-stage water budgets.
column4: Groundwater depletion across agricultural basins; higher pumping electricity costs; soil salinization.

column2: Delayed Crop Disease Diagnosis & Chemical Misuse
column3: Crop diseases (Paddy Blast, Banana Sigatoka, Sugarcane Red Rot, Groundnut Tikka) are diagnosed late. Farmers rely on unverified, indiscriminate chemical sprays that degrade soil microbiomes, enter groundwater, and build pathogen resistance.
column4: Annual crop losses of 25-35%; toxic chemical runoff into freshwater streams; high debt burden for smallholders.

column2: Suboptimal Crop Selection & Monoculture Soil Depletion
column3: Farmers repeatedly plant identical crops across adjacent fields without crop rotation or soil chemistry matching (pH, NPK), causing acute soil micronutrient exhaustion and severe yield declines.
column4: Declining soil fertility; increased pest vulnerability; economic vulnerability to single-crop market price crashes.

column3: Over 70% of marginal farmers do not access beneficial central/state schemes (PM-KISAN, PMFBY crop insurance, KCC, drip subsidies) due to lack of scheme awareness, complex eligibility criteria, and tedious documentation.
column4: Farmers take high-interest private loans from moneylenders, leading to severe financial stress.

column3: Existing agricultural tech platforms are cluttered with English text, complex technical jargon, and rigid desktop layouts, rendering them inaccessible to rural smallholders across diverse linguistic regions.
column4: High barrier to technological adoption; smallholder farmers are left behind in the digital transition.
